packet.description_seed: Former England captain and manager Kevin Keegan dies at the age of 75, seven weeks after he revealed he had been diagnosed with stage four cancer.

Keegan was diagnosed with stomach cancer in January and shared that the disease had spread to other parts of his body last month. It was announced on Monday that he had died. One of English football's all-time greats, Keegan won titles at Liverpool and Hamburger SV, and as a manager led Newcastle from the second division to the brink of Premier League glory and also took England to Euro 2000. FORMER ENGLAND AND Newcastle United manager Kevin Keegan has died at the age of 75. A statement shared on behalf of his family said: “It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. “The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments. Kevin Keegan has sadly passed away at the age of 75 following a battle with cancer, his family have announced.

It was confirmed back in January that the legendary former Newcastle manager was being treated for cancer, with Keegan himself revealing the disease was at stage four last month during an appearance at a fan event.

A statement released by Keegan's family on Monday afternoon read: "It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

"Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support. "This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

Kevin Keegan told fans at an appearance at the start of June that he had stage-four cancer, the most advanced stage of the disease.

Football great, who managed England and played for Liverpool, passes after battle with cancer

Liverpool and Newcastle football legend Kevin Keegan has died aged 75 after a career that saw him manage England and win two Ballon d'Ors.

Keegan was diagnosed with stomach cancer in January and shared that the disease had spread to other parts of his body last month.

It was announced on Monday that he had died.

One of English football's all-time greats, Keegan won titles at Liverpool and Hamburger SV, and as a manager led Newcastle from the second division to the brink of Premier League glory and also took England to Euro 2000.

But when asked by Peter Graves at an event in Tyne Theatre in June, he said he did not want a statue.

“My statue is the way people receive me," he said, adding that he had not been back to St James's Park since a dispute with the Newcastle board led to his departure as manager in 2009, his last job in football.

"You will have to wait until I die, I'm afraid," he added. "I'm not against the statues that are outside."

“I want to say goodbye. I didn’t get the chance when I left the club last time."

Here are the statistics around Kevin Keegan's career.

Football League First Division: 1972–73, 1975–76, 1976–77

British Home Championship: 1973, 1975, 1979, 1982

Newcastle 1992-1997: Win 55%, Draw 20%, Lose 25%

Keegan led Newcastle from Division 2 [the modern-day League 1] to the Premier League and challenged for the title in 1995-96, but lost out to Manchester United. He led the club in Europe the next season before resigning due to differences with the board.

Fulham 1998-1999: Win 62%, Draw 20%, Lose 18%

Keegan took over with Fulham in the third tier, he led the team to the second tier with the help of an impressive squad bankrolled by Harrods owner Mohamed Al-Fayed. He left in 1999 to become England manager.

England 1999-2000: Win 39%, Draw 39%, Lose 22%

His time with the national side was brief, managing to qualify for Euro 2000 but getting knocked out in the group stage. His final game in charge was a home defeat to Germany, the last match at the old Wembley.

Manchester City 2001-2005: Win 44%, Draw 22%, Lose 34%

Keegan immediately won promotion to the Premier League in his first season with City, where they have stayed ever since. He established them as a top-flight club before retiring from football in 2005.

payload.title: Jalkapallolegenda Kevin Keegan on kuollut 75-vuotiaana
payload.summary: Kevin Keegan on kuollut 75-vuotiaana syöpäsairauden jälkeen. Kaksinkertainen Ballon d'Or -voittaja menestyi Liverpoolissa ja Hamburger SV:ssä sekä valmensi Newcastlea ja Englannin maajoukkuetta.
payload.content:
Englantilaisen jalkapallon suuriin nimiin kuulunut Kevin Keegan on kuollut 75-vuotiaana. Entisen Englannin maajoukkuekapteenin ja päävalmentajan perhe vahvisti kuoleman maanantaina. Keegan sairasti syöpää ja kertoi kesäkuussa sairauden edenneen neljänteen vaiheeseen sekä levinneen muualle elimistöön.

## Perhe pyytää yksityisyyttä

Perheen julkaiseman lausunnon mukaan Keegan kuoli vaimonsa ja tyttäriensä ympäröimänä. Läheiset kuvasivat häntä rakastetuksi aviomieheksi, isäksi ja isoisäksi. He kiittivät Keegania hoitanutta lääkintähenkilöstöä tuesta ja pyysivät surun keskellä rauhaa sekä yksityisyyttä.

Keeganilla todettiin vatsasyöpä tammikuussa. Kesäkuussa hän kertoi julkisesti, että sairaus oli levinnyt muihin osiin hänen kehoaan ja edennyt neljänteen vaiheeseen.

## Menestystä Englannissa ja Saksassa

Keegan saavutti pelaajana suurta menestystä Liverpoolissa, jossa hän voitti mestaruuksia. Englannin ulkopuolella hän pelasi Hamburger SV:ssä ja voitti mestaruuksia myös saksalaisseuran riveissä. Henkilökohtaisen tunnustuksen huippuna hän sai urallaan kahdesti Ballon d'Or -palkinnon.

Englannin maajoukkueessa Keegan pelasi ja toimi kapteenina. Myöhemmin hän siirtyi valmennustehtäviin ja nousi myös maajoukkueen päävalmentajaksi. Hänen johdollaan Englanti osallistui vuoden 2000 EM-turnaukseen, joka jäi yhdeksi hänen näkyvimmistä tehtävistään maajoukkuevalmentajana.

Pitkä ura sekä kentällä että vaihtopenkin edessä teki Keeganista yhden englantilaisen jalkapallon tunnetuimmista hahmoista. Hänen saavutuksiinsa kuuluivat menestys kahdessa eri maassa sekä vastuu maajoukkueesta pelaajana ja valmentajana.

## Newcastlen kannattajien rakastama hahmo

Keegan muistetaan Newcastlessa myös pelaajana, mutta erityisen suuren jäljen hän jätti seuraan valmentajana. Hän johti seuraa kahdella eri jaksolla St James' Parkilla, nosti joukkueen Englannin toiselta sarjatasolta ja vei sen myöhemmin Valioliigan mestaruuden tuntumaan.

Newcastle sanoi olevansa kuolinuutisesta järkyttynyt. Seura kuvasi Keegania yhdeksi historiansa ikonisimmista, vaikutusvaltaisimmista ja rakastetuimmista henkilöistä. Seuran mukaan hän oli sukupolvien kannattajille enemmän kuin legendaarinen pelaaja ja valmentaja: hän oli Newcastle Unitedin sykkivä sydän.

Vielä kesäkuussa Keeganilta kysyttiin Newcastlen Tyne Theatre -tapahtumassa, haluaisiko hänelle pystytettävän patsaan. Hän vastasi, ettei halunnut sellaista.
summary_bullets: Perheen mukaan Keegan kuoli vaimonsa ja tyttäriensä ympäröimänä.
Hän voitti Ballon d'Or -palkinnon kahdesti ja mestaruuksia Liverpoolissa sekä Hamburger SV:ssä.
Valmentajana hän vei Newcastlen toiselta sarjatasolta lähelle Valioliigan mestaruutta ja Englannin vuoden 2000 EM-turnaukseen.

Newcastle sanoi olevansa kuolinuutisesta järkyttynyt. Seura kuvasi Keegania yhdeksi historiansa ikonisimmista, vaikutusvaltaisimmista ja rakastetuimmista henkilöistä. Seuran mukaan hän oli sukupolvien kannattajille enemmän kuin legendaarinen pelaaja ja valmentaja: hän oli Newcastle Unitedin sykkivä sydän.

Vielä kesäkuussa Keeganilta kysyttiin Newcastlen Tyne Theatre -tapahtumassa, haluaisiko hänelle pystytettävän patsaan. Hän vastasi, ettei halunnut sellaista.

Kevin Keegan(Image: (Liverpool FC via Getty Images)) Newcastle have released a statement saying that are "devastated" following the passing of Kevin Keegan. Keegan is a Magpies legend after two managerial stints at St James' Park. "We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club’s history," the statement read. "Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters." (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Images) We're sorry to bring you the desperately sad news that Kevin Keegan, the former Newcastle and England manager, has died at the age of 75. Keegan had been battling cancer. His family confirmed the sad news of his passing with a statement.

Football great, who managed England and played for Liverpool, passes after battle with cancer Liverpool and Newcastle football legend Kevin Keegan has died aged 75 after a career that saw him manage England and win two Ballon d'Ors. Keegan was diagnosed with stomach cancer in January and shared that the disease had spread to other parts of his body last month. It was announced on Monday that he had died. One of English football's all-time greats, Keegan won titles at Liverpool and Hamburger SV, and as a manager led Newcastle from the second division to the brink of Premier League glory and also took England to Euro 2000. But when asked by Peter Graves at an event in Tyne Theatre in June, he said he did not want a statue.

FORMER ENGLAND AND Newcastle United manager Kevin Keegan has died at the age of 75. A statement shared on behalf of his family said: “It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. “The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments. Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. “The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy.” In June, Keegan shared that he had stage four cancer. It came six months after his family first announced that he had been diagnosed with cancer. ---
